intended_object: The functor of points, on commutative R-algebras, of the closed subgroup scheme of GL_n defined by a Hopf ideal I in the coordinate ring of GL_n, realised as matrices. It sends A to the subgroup of GL_n(A) of points that vanish on I, and sends an algebra map to the map that applies it to each matrix entry. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
How the functor is built:
- **On objects**, it sends A to `hopfIdealPointsSubgroup n I A`. This is the image in GL_n(A) of the A-valued Hopf-algebra points (algebra maps O(GL_n) → A) that vanish on I. The lemma `mem_hopfIdealPointsSubgroup_iff` confirms membership is exactly "the corresponding point kills I".
- **On morphisms**, it uses `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map`, restricted to these subgroups, which applies the algebra map to each entry.
- **Universe lift:** `GrpCat.uliftFunctor` only lifts the universe so the codomain matches the generic points functor. It does not change the group.

The same file builds a natural isomorphism, `hopfIdealPointsSubgroupNatIso`, between this functor and the points functor of the quotient Hopf algebra O(GL_n)/I. This confirms it is the functor of points of the closed subgroup scheme V(I) ⊂ GL_n.

**Generality:** the base ring R is any commutative ring, n is any natural number, and the inputs are all commutative R-algebras, so nothing is restricted. The matrix description only makes sense for GL_n, which is the purpose of this definition. The general version (points of any quotient Hopf algebra) exists separately in the library. I did not find a Mathlib definition of this functor.
